text:
Jordan: Heads-up — seeing a weird ECC/Xid spike on rack26 since last night's driver roll. Not the usual pattern (short bursts across multiple cards), looks like a correlated noise pattern.

Alisa: Ack. Any heat/thermal alerts from the PDUs?

Jordan: No PDU deltas. Temps steady ~42C. Kernel logs show repeated patterns: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=8421 pcie_read..
[ 1234.568001] NVRM: GPU 0: CE count increased to 14
[ 1235.001234] nvidia: ecc error detected, channel parity mismatch
```
Not typical ECC drift. Also see the same signature across GPUs 0,2,5 in the rack.

Mike: Interesting — same firmware bundle deployed to rack24/26/29 last night, right? @infra-bot what was the rollout batch id?

infra-bot: Rollout complete: fw-driver-2026.03.14-rc3 applied to racks [24,26,29] between 02:17-02:44 UTC. Canary rate 5% -> 100% after automated checks.

Sophie: @Jordan can you paste `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,ERR` from one of the affected hosts? Might help see if CE counts are persistent per card.

Jordan: Pasting from host rack26-node07: 
```
==============GPU 0000:65:00:00==============
Ecc Errors (Volatile):
  Single-bit ECC errors: 14
  Double-bit ECC errors: 0
  Volatile GPU ECC: 14
==============GPU 0000:67:00:00==============
Ecc Errors (Volatile):
  Single-bit ECC errors: 13
```
They tick up ~1-2 every few minutes under idle. Not under load.

Ivan: That smells like a signal integrity issue or a bad batch trace, especially if it affects the same PCI lanes across boards. Any serial correlation?

Jordan: I pulled serial prefixes: GPU serials all share prefix A9-3B4-XX for the affected cohort (cards across 6 chassis).

Alisa: If it’s a manufacturing trace we should quarantine the serial range. But first, can we rule out PCI riser / backplane? Any nvlink/PCI resets?

Mike: No nvlink faults. I checked BMC logs — no FRU events. Also swapped one GPU from node07 into node02 (known-good backplane) and still saw CE climb on that card after ~30m. Swap confirms card moves the fault.

Sophie: Good repro. That pushes it to a card-level issue. Next steps: 1) Quarantine serial prefix A9-3B4-*, 2) Open RMA with vendor with logs and CE timelines, 3) Schedule targeted drain of affected nodes to avoid production evictions.

Jordan: Agreed. I'll tag affected hosts and schedule a rolling drain tonight 0200-0400 UTC. Also capturing kernel trace on one card for vendor.

Ivan: Cost note — if we RMA the whole cohort, that's ~18 GPUs across three racks. We should calculate thermal/capacity hit for Dedicated pools and notify capacity team.

Alisa: I'll prepare capacity impact doc and temporary soft-quota to prevent heavy workloads from landing on those racks until replacement.

Mike: For the RCA: possible causes = manufacturing batch marginality, correlated driver/firmware sensitivity, or subtle board-level change in recent assembly run. Vendor convo should include: serial list, firmware version, kernel logs, and swap repro steps.

Jordan: I'll attach the logs and the swap timeline to the ticket. Quick mitigation: enable ECC scrub more frequently on affected hosts and apply a kernel udev rule to cordon GPUs with CE rate > 5/hour. Anyone object?

Sophie: No objections. Implement the scrub + cordon rule as a short-term policy. Add an alert to pager if CE rate crosses threshold for >30m.

infra-bot: Incident ticket INF-2026-042 created for "Entropy signature ECC wave — rack26 cohort". Assigned: Jordan, Sophie. Priority: P2.

Jordan: Thanks. I'll update this thread after RMA vendor reply and after the drain window tonight. :thumbsup:
